A very dry pattern is now entrenched across the Marianas, with only
spotty light showers evident on the latest radar data. Typhoon In-fa
is seen to the east-northeast of Saipan, moving steadily toward the
northern CNMI. However, convection and the wind field remain close to
the center. Therefore, not expecting to see much activity south of
Alamagan. Over the next week, POPs will range from 0 to 20 percent
across the Marianas. For Sunday and Monday, light and variable winds
will allow island convection to develop over Guam and possibly the
CNMI. By Tuesday, winds look to be a bit stronger, decreasing the
likelihood of island effect showers. 

Marine/Surf...
For the marine forecast, large, long-period northeast swell emanating
from TY In-fa will result in a quick increase in seas over the
region, with Tinian and Saipan waters seeing seas up to 14 feet,
especially over the northeast waters, and Rota and Guam seeing seas
of 10 feet. Altimetry data confirms seas up to 16 feet well east of
the waters. Seas are expected to exceed 10 feet across the region
shortly after midnight tonight, peaking during the evening Friday.
Seas will then begin to subside, likely dropping below 10 feet 
Saturday morning. As the seas build, expect increasing surf heights
as well. Surf could build as high as 18 feet along north and east
facing reefs of Tinian and Saipan, and up to 14 feet for Rota and
Guam. This surf will result in a high risk of dangerous rip currents
Friday through Saturday. Minor coastal inundation is possible along 
north and east facing reefs of Tinian and Saipan as well. Gentle to 
moderate winds will continue for Tinian and Saipan, with mostly 
gentle winds for Guam and Rota.

Tropical Systems...
As of 4:00 PM ChST earlier today, Typhoon In-fa (30W) was located 
near 15.9N 154.6E and moving west at 18 MPH. In-fa is expected to 
make a slight turn to the west-northwest through Friday before 
turning northwest early Saturday morning. Maximum sustained winds 
decreased to 130 MPH, still remaining a Category 4 typhoon, and will 
maintain this intensity as it passes near or over Agrihan of the 
northern CNMI Friday evening. Once In-fa emerges west of the 
Marianas, maximum sustained winds may gradually decrease, potentially
becoming a Category 3 typhoon Saturday afternoon as it makes a sharp
turn to the west towards the Philippine Sea. Damaging winds of at 
least 39 MPH are expected within the next 24 hours at Agrihan, Pagan,
and Alamagan, with typhoon conditions of 74 MPH winds or more also 
expected. As such, the previously issued Typhoon Watch was upgraded 
to a Typhoon Warning for these three islands. As for Guam, Rota, 
Tinian, and Saipan, a southward shift in In-fa's track is always 
possible, but direct impacts remain highly unlikely at this time.

For more information on Typhoon In-fa, please refer to bulletins 
from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN31 PGTW
and from the National Weather Service under WMO headers WTPQ31 
PGUM and WTPQ81 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
Pohnpei will see a short period of scattered showers and light to
gentle southwesterlies tonight with limited convection as cross-
equatorial winds flowing into Typhoon In-fa moves through the area, 
mainly concentrated to the west. Kosrae sits within broad, 
anticyclonic flow, bringing isolated showers and light to gentle 
variable winds tonight. This pattern will encompass Pohnpei, so 
light and variable winds and isolated showers are to be expected
Friday. Majuro is situated within northwesterly convergence, so 
scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms are forecast tonight 
through Friday before this feature eventually moves west and 
dissipates. Then, ridging will occur over all three forecast points,
so isolated showers and light to gentle winds of differing 
directions will prevail through the rest of the forecast period, with
the possible exception of Kosrae from Saturday night through Tuesday
as a fragment of the monsoon trough potentially re-establishes 
itself nearby.

Benign seas will continue through this weekend with swells out of the
northwest and southeast for Pohnpei and Kosrae, and out of the east 
for Majuro. Then, distant mid-latitude features may send a long- 
period, slightly elevated north swell to the region next week. 
Combined seas could stay below hazardous criteria, but surf heights 
along north and east facing reefs may warrant advisories. Those with 
marine interests should remain updated with the forecast over the 
next several days.

Western Micronesia...
Typhoon In-fa is well north of Chuuk, with only spotty showers
extending into northern Chuuk State due to modest convergence along 
the gentle to moderate southwesterly flow. As In-fa moves northwest,
